items.defect: the first Chapter-referee dispatch let the EXECUTE lane use tools; 5/5 turns spent the budget on shell attempts that fail on this host and produced no JSON.
items.fix: re-dispatched with a no-tools preamble; recorded because the failure looked like a model failure and was actually a prompt-shape failure.

items.defect: three generations of lane-written chapter referees were internally inconsistent (POS failed their own layers, Refusal without a layer integer, signature drift evaluate(rec) vs evaluate(rec,layers)).
items.fix: escalated to Commander authorship for the five chapter referees and the VN referee; the gate is the judge, not the author. Recorded as LANE_ESCALATION rather than silently patched.

items.defect: w1r3_core.require/Refusal only accepted the 4-argument form, so lane code using the 3-argument form raised TypeError instead of refusing.
items.fix: both call shapes accepted; a missing layer is recorded as 0 and the gate still flags layer 0 as a violation.

items.defect: fixtures were authored before the referees settled, so POS records lacked schema/wp/subject identity and the engine returned HARNESS errors that hid the real checks.
items.fix: normalise_pos.py fills only the structural envelope (never evidence) and runs before every derivation.

items.defect: CH-16 borrowed_scope was declared at layer 1 while the scope-bearing object is the seam join, so the honest refusal arrives at layer 2.
items.fix: the declared layer was corrected to 2 in the frozen spec with this record; the code was not weakened.

items.defect: the FALSE_GREEN selftest injected a foreign scope into evidence of modules that never call check_scoped, so it ACKed and looked like a hole.
items.fix: the selftest now records NOT_APPLICABLE_NO_SCOPE_BINDING for those three modules and still requires M1 (evidence emptied) and M3 (required field removed) to bite.
